Practised multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000 using place value; 1 unaided response was correct.
Practised mental multiplication using doubling and halving, including 25 × 16 and 50 × 8.
Sameer doubled both factors in one method, giving 50 × 32; this mix-up was not corrected by the end.

end.parentNote: Sameer practised place-value multiplication and mental multiplication through doubling and halving. They correctly explained that 3 groups of 10 make 30 and worked through 50 × 18 as 5 × 18, then adding a zero. The main mix-up was doubling both factors instead of doubling one and halving the other; this was still present at the end. At home, practise a few examples such as 25 × 16 by saying aloud: “double 25, halve 16,” then check the product.
